section_1.title: The Problem of Changing Velocity
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental conflict: Geometry measures static shapes, but the real world is constantly moving. Establish the prerequisite: Understanding that Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time.
section_1.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle. The cheetah doesn't run at a constant speed; its velocity changes every millisecond. How do we measure its 'exact' speed at a single moment?

section_2.title: The Method of Exhaustion (Limits)
section_2.content: Introduce the core concept of the 'Limit'. Explain that by shrinking the time interval toward zero, we reach the instantaneous rate of change.
section_2.example: Visual animation: Zooming in on the cheetah’s position graph. As the time window shrinks from 1 second to 0.1s, then 0.001s, the secant line (connecting two points) converges into a tangent line.

section_3.title: Differential Calculus: The Power of Slicing
section_3.content: Define the Derivative as the 'slope of the curve'. It is the mathematical tool for analyzing change at a precise point in time.
section_3.example: A drone adjusting its propeller speed. The derivative tells the drone's computer exactly how much power to increase at that exact instant to remain stable in a gust of wind.

section_4.title: Integral Calculus: The Art of Summation
section_4.content: Introduce Integration as the inverse process: instead of slicing, we accumulate. We sum up an infinite number of infinitesimal parts to find total quantities like area or displacement.
section_4.example: Visual animation: Filling a weirdly shaped pond with water. We treat the pond as millions of thin, rectangular strips. By summing these strips, we calculate the exact volume of water.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
section_5.content: Conclude by revealing the 'Grand Unification': Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like addition and subtraction, just at the scale of infinity.
section_5.example: The Cheetah Wrap-up: If we know the cheetah's instantaneous velocity (Derivative) at every moment, we can 'sum' them up (Integral) to find the total distance covered during the entire hunt.

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
